Data.subject: Education, Language Spoken and Literacy
Data.title: Government Expenditure On Education, Annual
Data.datasource: MINISTRY OF EDUCATION AND MINISTRY OF FINANCE
Data.footnote: Data refer to the financial year which begins in April and ends in March of the following year.  Data for FY2026 are budgeted estimates. Data for FY2025 are revised estimates.

row.footnote: Prior to 1981, figures include Expenditure of Adult Education Board.

Refers to National University of Singapore, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore Management University, Singapore University of Social Sciences, Singapore University of Technology and Design (with effect from FY2008) and Singapore Institute of Technology (with effect from FY2009).  1991 figures include one time endowment fund of $250 million each to National University of Singapore and Nanyang Technological University.
National Institute of Education (NIE), formed in July 1991 by merging Institute of Education and College of Physical Education, is part of Nanyang Technological University.
Refers to Singapore Polytechnic, Ngee Ann Polytechnic, Temasek Polytechnic, Nanyang Polytechnic and Republic Polytechnic.

Data includes MOE Headquarters, ISEAS - Yusof Ishak Institute and Science Centre Board.  Data for Institute of Technical Education, Tertiary and Others include budget for Continuing Education Training (CET) grants disbursed by Ministry of Education (MOE).  With effect from FY1999, data includes Special Education, Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts, LASALLE College of the Arts.  With effect from FY2003, data include Singapore Examinations and Assessment Board.  With effect from FY2016, data include SkillsFuture Singapore Agency except for CET grants disbursed by MOE.

row.rowText: Proportion Of Government Expenditure On Education To GDP
row.footnote: Data are based on financial year.  The total expenditure estimates do not include Special Transfers and spending from Government Endowment and Trust Funds.  Data may differ from previous years due to revisions to GDP estimates.  Updates are also available from the 'Analysis of Revenue and Expenditure' webpage of Singapore's Ministry of Finance Budget Website.
